niche_preference_profile: This user most consistently prefers interfaces with strong spacing control and clear hierarchy, usually favoring fewer competing elements, generous whitespace, and simplified compositions. They often like soft, rounded shapes, pill buttons, and gentler visual treatments over sharp or rigid ones. They frequently prefer layouts that make actions and structure obvious through grouped cards, modular sections, centered focal points, and visible primary CTAs. Their color preferences are mixed by context, but they repeatedly favor softer, more controlled contrast and dislike harsh, noisy, or visually aggressive treatments. They also tend to prefer concise, digestible content presentation with summaries, labels, and scannable structure instead of dense uninterrupted text. In several cases they favor richer guidance and more visible functionality when it improves clarity, but not when it creates clutter.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers sparse or moderately simplified layouts with generous whitespace, breathing room, and fewer competing elements; rejects crowded, busy, tightly packed screens.

Prefers clearly organized layouts with grouped sections, modular cards, centered focal points, and strong emphasis on the main content or action; rejects weak hierarchy or attention split across many areas.

Prefers controlled color palettes and softer contrast treatments, often in dark themes but sometimes light themes when readability is improved; rejects harsh, overly intense, noisy, or low-visibility color treatments.
Prefers soft rounded cards, large corner radii, pill-shaped buttons, and generally gentler visual styling; rejects squarer, sharper, more rigid presentation.

Prefers concise, digestible information shown through summaries, bullets, labeled fields, segmented cards, or compact scannable rows; rejects long text blocks, legal-style reading burden, or poorly chunked information.
Prefers visible, prominent, clearly labeled actions such as bottom toolbars, strong primary CTAs, top-level controls, and obvious decision points; rejects hidden, weak, or ambiguous action patterns.

Prefers interfaces that provide helpful context such as onboarding support, search/filter tools, placeholders, password rules, metadata, and explanatory structure when these improve usability; rejects sparse guidance that leaves the next step unclear.
